title: Partakers of divine nature; new man in true holiness
source_text: VIII. Huc quoque spectat quod fideles dicuntur θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως, divinae consortes naturae, & lapsi ex corruptione, quae est in mundo per cupiditatem, 2 Pet. 1. 4. Item a peccatis abluti, sanctificati, purgati, & induti novo homine, qui creatus est secundum Deum in justitia & sanctitate veritatis, 1 Cor. 6. 11. Act. 20. 32. quique renovatur in agnitionem secundum imaginem ejus qui creavit illum, Ephes. 4. 24. Quibus verbis aperte tribuitur justitia & sanctimonia, & quidem non ficta & appa-rens tantum, sed realis & vera, & in qua sanctitatis & justitiae divinae imago quae-dam reluceat; adeoque cujus ratione fideles divinae quodammodo naturae participes fiunt.
pass_a_gloss: To this also belongs the fact that believers are said to be partakers of the divine nature, and to have escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust (2 Peter 1:4); likewise washed from sins, sanctified, purged, and clothed with the new man who is created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth (1 Corinthians 6:11; Acts 20:32), and who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of him who created him (Ephesians 4:24). By which words righteousness and sanctity are openly ascribed—and indeed not feigned and apparent only, but real and true, and such that in it a certain image of divine holiness and righteousness shines; and therefore by reason of it believers become in a certain way partakers of the divine nature.
pass_b_english: Believers are partakers of the divine nature; washed, sanctified, clothed with the new man in true justice and holiness.
This righteousness is real, not feigned—an image of divine holiness.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1042.
